text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thank you for getting in touch about your father, and I'm sorry for your loss. I'll keep a running list of everyone's concerns in one place, so we can all see it.

Here is the list as it stands:

1. C does not agree to sell the house to A and her husband at a family discount.
2. C thinks B could use some of the money from the house.

I'm writing to A and B now to hear what they want. I cannot make legal decisions or move money for you, but I can help the three of you work out a plan you can take to a lawyer.

Two questions for you. What would you like to see happen with the house? And has anyone read the will with a lawyer yet?

I’m fine with A buying the house, but not at a family discount that costs me my fair share. I’d like us to settle it fairly, but there’s no rush. I don’t know whether anyone has reviewed the will with a lawyer.

I hope to buy the house with my husband, but I know C hasn’t agreed. By a family discount, I mean below market value; no price or terms have been settled. I’m not sure the will has been reviewed with a lawyer.

Good news: all three of you are open to you buying the house. The open question is price and terms, not whether the sale happens. Here is the updated list.

2. C thinks B could use some money from the house.
3. A wants to buy the house with her husband below market value. No price and no terms have been agreed.
4. B would like the house to provide money toward starting a dance studio. B is open to A buying it if the terms are fair to all three.
5. No one has had the will reviewed with a lawyer.

Two steps I suggest. First, get one independent valuation of the house so you all work from the same number. Second, have a lawyer read the will, because the will sets out who owns what and how a sale can happen.

I cannot make legal decisions or move money. I can keep the list and help you agree the questions to put to the lawyer. Would you agree to both steps?
